description: An eight-block sequencer with seven ways to evolve what it is playing, each on a button and a trigger input

params.text: One beat of the sequence, holding up to four notes in one of nine subdivisions; left click to step forward, shift and left click to step back, right click to choose from a list
Sets the pitch of one note in the block: click for a keyboard carrying Rest, Tie and an Auto Advance button, or drag up and down to set the voltage
Sets how many note blocks are played before the sequence returns to the first
Switches the sequence between playing forward and playing in reverse
Switches the inversion on and off, turning the distance between each note played upside down
Shifts the blocks of the sequence one position forward or backward
Gives the next block to be played a fresh set of random pitches
Copies the rhythm of another block onto the next block to be played
Adds a note to the next block to be played, or takes one away
Gives the next block to be played a fresh random rhythm
Takes every evolution back off, returning the sequence to what was programmed

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one note block
Returns the sequence to its first note block when the voltage rises past 2V
Switches the sequence between forward and reverse when the voltage rises past 2V
Switches the inversion on and off when the voltage rises past 2V
Shifts the blocks one position when the voltage rises past 2V
Gives the next block fresh random pitches when the voltage rises past 2V
Copies another block's rhythm onto the next block when the voltage rises past 2V
Adds or removes a note in the next block when the voltage rises past 2V
Gives the next block a fresh random rhythm when the voltage rises past 2V
Takes every evolution back off when the voltage rises past 2V

outputs.text: High while a note is playing, for the length set on the menu
The pitch of the note now playing
A gate at the end of each cycle

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
the evolutions are an overlay on the programmed sequence, so the Clear button puts everything back rather than undoing one step at a time
menu: Permitted Rhythm Evolutions — chooses which subdivisions the borrow, mutate and random evolutions are allowed to use
Fill Remaining Sequence — fills every note block outside the current length at random, using the blocks that are inside it
Invert Mode: Semitones, Quantize, Steps — measures the inverted interval in semitones, in semitones then quantised to the note pool, or in steps through the note pool
Gate Length — sets how much of each note the gate output stays high for
Swing — delays every second note block
Clock Mode: Gate, Phase — reads the clock input either as a square wave, high above 2V and low below 0.1V, or as a ramp that advances a block when it falls from above 9V to below 1V
Randomize — randomises the pitches or the rhythm of the whole sequence
Shift & Shuffle — shifts and shuffles the sequence from the menu, the way the Shift & Shuffle expander does from its jacks
Set Rhythm — sets every note block to one subdivision
Note Pool — sets the pool of notes the randomisers draw from, from a scale, from a keyboard, or by shifting the current pool in semitones
Copy/Paste — copies and pastes the sequence or the note pool in a portable format that other JP sequencers read
Expanders — places an expander module beside this one
